author: gmalbert
body:
This pull request introduces probability calibration for horse racing predictions to address the issue of overconfident win probabilities produced by the XGBoost model. The main enhancement is the implementation of a shrinkage calibration method, which compresses predicted probabilities toward a realistic range, resulting in more accurate and interpretable outputs. Supporting documentation and test scripts are also included to justify the approach and compare alternatives.

**Probability Calibration Implementation:**

- Added shrinkage calibration to `scripts/predict_todays_races.py`, applying the formula `(raw + prior*k) / (1 + k)` (with `prior = 1/field_size`, `k=3.5`) to compress win probabilities toward the field average. This results in realistic probability ranges for favorites and longshots, and updates the calculation of place/show probabilities based on the calibrated win probability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-993064f5a44053d84aaf3720ba9e1a56c6488378e6855bbd7b28e5a6525ec85bR8-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-993064f5a44053d84aaf3720ba9e1a56c6488378e6855bbd7b28e5a6525ec85bR295) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-993064f5a44053d84aaf3720ba9e1a56c6488378e6855bbd7b28e5a6525ec85bL310-R372)

**Documentation and Justification:**

- Added `tmp/calibration_summary.md`, summarizing the calibration problem, solution, before/after statistics, and validation of results. This document demonstrates that the new probabilities are in line with real-world expectations and betting markets.
- Added `tmp/calibration_options.py`, providing an overview and code for several calibration methods (temperature scaling, Platt scaling, isotonic regression, beta calibration, shrinkage) with recommendations for immediate and future improvements.

**Testing and Comparison:**

- Added `tmp/test_calibration.py`, a script to compare calibration methods (temperature scaling and shrinkage) on actual prediction data, outputting per-race and overall statistics to guide parameter selection and validate calibration effectiveness.

## Summary
This PR fixes pricing calculation and display issues in the quote detail view by ensuring calculations run regardless of sidebar visibility and using live calculation data instead of stale database values.

- **Auto-calculate pricing when sidebar is collapsed**: Added a new `useEffect` hook that triggers pricing calculations via the `/api/quotes/{id}/calculate` endpoint when the sidebar is closed. - **Fix material name display**: Updated the material name rendering to use the nested `piece.materials?.name` property when available, falling back to `piece.material_name` and then to '-' if neither exists.

## Implementation Details
- The auto-calculation effect includes proper cleanup (cancellation flag) to prevent state updates on unmounted components
- The effect depends on `mode`, `editLoading`, `sidebarOpen`, `quoteIdStr`, `refreshTrigger`, and `handleCalculationUpdate` to ensure it recalculates when relevant state changes
- The piece breakdown lookup uses the `pieceId` to match calculation results with individual pieces

author: jacquerel
body:
## About The Pull Request

I believe this is the night's first "post-maintainer round" PR.
Some people got really confused in a round I just played after they killed me because I was using the ghost species and I had activated the ghost wallwalking ability.

Post-death, my corpse still could not be removed from the immediate area of my gravestone in order to be gibbed or thrown into the supermatter or whatever it was they were planning to do with it, which greatly confused them.
Following this, once they dug up my grave the skeleton it spawned had a different name than me which further led my killers to believe that I was going to return as a lich, and in fact they weren't even sure if that skeleton was my corpse at all (technically it wasn't I guess).

Additionally, every item that had been on my person was destroyed, which I think is mostly just unintended.

Finally, I noticed in testing that if I possessed someone else and dug up my (former) own grave it would put me back into the dead skeleton, which we probably don't want.

So:
- Ghosts now automatically return to their grave if they're killed in passthrough mode, leaving a ghost corpse at the former location of the gravestone.
- The skeleton that can be dug out of a ghost's grave now has that ghost's name, and additionally all of their worldly belongings were buried in the grave and spill out onto the ground.
- You will only have your ghost pulled into the skeleton corpse if your grave is dug up while you are flying around and alive.

## Changelog

:cl:
fix: Dead ghosts will return to the grave upon dying.
fix: When you dig up a ghost's grave you will find the skeleton of that ghost, not the skeleton of some other random guy.
fix: The grave will also contain all of the ghost's worldly belongings.
/:cl:

author: letstakeawalk
body: ## Summary `preview_hunk` was the only hunk command that did not support greedy. When navigating with `nav_hunk` (which defaults to `greedy=true`) and `diff_opts.linematch` enabled, `preview_hunk` shows linematch-split hunks individually while `preview_hunk_inline` correctly shows the merged diff. This causes inconsistent preview behavior between the two commands. ## Steps to reproduce Given a file with the following content committed: ```markdown - [ ] lorem ipsum - [ ] add line below and change me - [ ] change me - [ ] lorem ipsum - [ ] lorem ipsum - [ ] delete me - [ ] change me - [ ] delete me - [ ] change me - [ ] lorem ipsum ``` Then changed to: ```markdown - [ ] lorem ipsum - [x] add line below and change me - [ ] new line - [x] change me - [ ] lorem ipsum - [ ] lorem ipsum - [x] change me - [x] change me - [ ] lorem ipsum ``` ### Before 1. Cursor at line 1 2. `nav_hunk("next")` → cursor at line 2 3. `preview_hunk()` Note: preview title shows `Hunk 1 of 7` 4. `preview_hunk_inline()` Note the difference 5. `nav_hunk("next")` → cursor at line 7 6. `preview_hunk()` Note: preview title shows `Hunk 5 of 7` 7. `preview_hunk_inline()` Note the difference `preview_hunk_inline` shows the diff as expected according to greedy `nav_hunk`, but `preview_hunk` only shows the individual linematch-split hunk. ### After (with this PR) `preview_hunk` now shows the same merged result as `preview_hunk_inline`, with the correct greedy hunk count in the title (`Hunk 1 of 2` and `Hunk 2 of 2`). ## Changes - **Refactor `get_hunk_with_staged`** to return hunk index and count - **Add greedy option to `preview_hunk`** — make it async, use `get_hunk_with_staged` and `Util.noautocmd` - **Add greedy option to `preview_hunk_inline`** — parameterize the hardcoded `true` - **Pass greedy from `nav_hunk`** to both preview functions - **Update generated docs**

## What
Show all tokens with non-zero balances by default when running `node balance.js`

## Why  
Currently users need to pass `--all` flag to see their full portfolio. Most users want to see all their holdings at a glance, not just ETH.

## Change
One line change in balance.js:
- Before: `if (args.all) {`
- After: `if (args.all || !args.token) {`

Tested locally, works as expected.

author: quciet
body:
### Motivation
- Ensure the renderer can re-attach to an in-progress ML Optimization run after reload/crash without restarting the Python process by persisting minimal job state and validated paths in the Electron main process.
- Keep the ML process (same PID) running across renderer reloads while letting a newly loaded renderer receive live logs/progress.

### Description
- Expanded the main-process `mlJobState` in `desktop/main.js` to include `ifsPath`, `ifsValidated`, `inputExcelPath`, `outputDir`, `runConfig`, and `lastUpdateAt`, and added `getSafeMLJobState()` and `updateMLJobContext()` helpers to safely expose and update that context.
- Wired validation handler (`validate-ifs-folder`) to update persisted UI context on each validation attempt, marking `ifsValidated` on success and storing input/output paths and base year info.
- Updated `run-ml` handling to populate the job snapshot before spawn (PID, timestamps, runConfig), update progress/error/lastUpdateAt as stdout/stderr arrives, and continue sending logs/progress to the current renderer via `mainWindow.webContents.send` (`sendToRenderer`) so a reloaded UI can resume receiving events.
- Added an IPC handler `ml:jobStatus` returning a safe snapshot (no giant logs) of the persisted state for renderer hydration.
- Updated frontend `App.tsx` and `global.d.ts` so the renderer calls `getMLJobStatus()` on mount, hydrates validated paths/config/progress into its local state, auto-opens the Tune page when a validated run is active, and passes an `initialRunConfig` to the Tune page so it can render correctly after reload.

### Testing
- Built the frontend with `npm run build` (in `frontend`) and the build completed successfully.
- Performed a basic main-process syntax check with `node --check desktop/main.js` which succeeded with no syntax errors.
- Started the dev frontend (`vite`) and exercised the running UI with an automated Playwright script, successfully capturing a screenshot of the app in the reloaded state (Firefox run succeeded; Chromium attempt failed in the CI environment due to browser sandbox/host limitations).
